ds: Inherent-risk factors seen during onboarding and refresh that suggest false, altered or reused identity information. Covers document fraud, inconsistent details, fictitious addresses and identifiers shared across unrelated customers.

src.t: FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach (sector-specific guidance series, general principles)
FATF Recommendations, Recommendation 1 and Interpretive Note (assessing risks and applying a risk-based approach)
Wolfsberg Group, Guidance on a Risk Based Approach for Managing Money Laundering Risks (2006)

cn.rt: Cross-cutting risk factor; applies across all consumer products and channels. Identity document integrity at onboarding.

rat: Identity document fraud seen at onboarding, remote and in-person.

ind.n: Suspected forged or altered identity document
ind.cx: Document shows signs of tampering, font or layout anomalies, or fails security-feature checks.
ind.fp: Worn or poorly scanned genuine documents can fail checks.
ind.ds: Identity document or selfie shows alteration, font or layout anomalies, or fails security-feature or forensic checks (including deepfake or injection artefacts).
ind.cn: Identity document tampering or forensic failure

ind.cx: Names, dates of birth or addresses differ between documents or from the application.
ind.fp: Transliteration, marriage name changes and typos are common.
ind.ds: Names, dates of birth, addresses or national ID numbers differ between documents, bureaux or the application.
ind.cn: Inconsistent personal details across documents or sources

ind.cx: Address does not exist, is a mail drop, or fails verification against authoritative data.
ind.fp: New builds and rural addresses may not be in databases.
ind.ds: Address does not exist, is a mail drop, or fails verification against authoritative data.

ind.cx: Same phone, email, address, device or ID number appears across multiple unrelated customers.
ind.fp: Families and shared households legitimately share details.
ind.ds: Same phone, email, address, device or ID number appears across multiple unrelated customers or users.

ind.cx: Thin or newly created credit and digital footprint, mixed attributes from different real persons.
ind.fp: Young or recently arrived people have thin files.
ind.ds: Thin or recently created credit and digital footprint, with mixed attributes suggesting a fabricated identity.
ind.cn: Synthetic identity with thin or newly created footprint

ind.cx: Same image or document submitted for different applicants or after previous rejection.
ind.fp: Resubmission after a poor-quality upload is legitimate.
ind.ds: Same document image, selfie, template, font or background appears across different applicants or after rejection.
ind.cn: Documents or images reused or templated across applicants

ind.cx: Applicant offers documents of limited reliability or unusual types without explanation.
ind.ds: Applicant offers documents of limited reliability or unusual types without explanation.

ind.n: Applicant details match watchlist or fraud record
ind.cx: Application data matches known fraud, mule or exited-customer records.
ind.ds: Application data matches known fraud, mule or exited-customer records.

ind.cx: Customer or intermediary urges bypassing checks or relies on personal connections.
ind.ds: Customer or intermediary urges rapid completion, secrecy or bypassing of checks, or leans on personal connections.
ind.cn: Pressure to speed up or bypass checks

ind.n: Signature or contact details differ on later instructions
ind.cx: Later instructions carry signatures or contact details that depart from onboarding records.
ind.ds: Later instructions carry signatures or contact details that depart from onboarding records.

ctl.n: Duplicate and synthetic identity checks at onboarding
ctl.ds: Compares new applicant identifiers such as name, email, phone, address, device and bank account with existing customers, previously declined or exited applicants and known-bad data. Matches are blocked or referred, limiting repeat applicants, synthetic identities and mule recruitment.

Remote verification of a person's identity using document capture, biometric matching and liveness or anti-spoofing checks, or a trusted digital identity. It reduces impersonation, synthetic identities and account opening with stolen or fabricated credentials.

Checks identity and supporting documents for tampering, forgery, template reuse and internal inconsistency, and corroborates their data against authoritative or reliable independent sources. It exposes altered or counterfeit credentials that pass a visual check.

Validates a stated address against postal or reference data, requires recent independent proof of residence or premises, and flags known mass-registration or virtual-office addresses. It supports identity assurance and helps reveal fictitious or shared addresses.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.

Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.

ctl.n: Alert adjudication standards and quality assurance
ctl.ds: Defines documented criteria for clearing or escalating screening and monitoring alerts, resolves matches using secondary identifiers and samples closed alerts for quality. It makes decisions consistent, defensible and auditable.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.

Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.

ctl.n: Senior management approval and risk acceptance
ctl.ds: Requires named senior management or a committee to approve onboarding, continuation or waivers for higher-risk relationships, with documented mitigations and periodic re-approval. It adds accountability and an independent challenge to risk acceptance.
Verifies instructions, detail changes and unusual requests by contacting the customer on a channel held on file, never one supplied in the request. It defeats impersonation and account takeover.
